notes: The certified 181-tag talent ontology remains the starting semantic vocabulary.
Owner-authorized skill-completeness rule expands the shared cross-domain ontology by six missing canonical skill tags.
Current approved shared vocabulary count is 187.
Prerequisite-only skill mentions remain non-semantic and do not add a skill tag.
If a Benefit/Special/Normal rule directly uses, modifies, substitutes, rerolls, accelerates, resists, or otherwise mechanically interacts with a specific skill, that skill tag is required.
A deterministic bounded ability-based skill family may expand to each affected skill tag (for example Strength-based -> Climb, Jump, Swim).
Effects applying generically to any/all skills use `skills` rather than receiving every individual skill tag.

Named examples inside a generic all-skills effect do not create a false specialization (for example Intimidator remains generic `skills` rather than becoming a Force feat merely because Use the Force is explicitly included among all skill checks).
Publication category, prerequisites, sourcebook identity, and semantic tags remain separate concerns.
Tech Specialist is one canonical feat identity whose primary publication is Saga Edition Web Enhancement 1 p.3; Starships of the Galaxy p.21 is a full reprint.

assignments.name: Starship Designer
assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Allows designing starships from scratch, removes the nonstandard-modification treatment for starship work, and enables repeated custom starship-system modifications including emplacement capacity, hull, hyperdrive, shields, and weapon accuracy.
assignments.existingTagsAuthority: data/feat_buckets_and_subbuckets.json metadataTags on current default branch; informational only, not semantic authority

rationale.tech: The Benefit creates and customizes advanced starship technology.
rationale.mechanics: The Benefit itself repeatedly uses Mechanics checks for design and custom modifications; this is not prerequisite-only inference.
rationale.crafting: The feat explicitly enables designing a starship from scratch and conducting extended fabrication/customization work.
rationale.modification: The feat alters starship systems and explicitly grants custom modifications.
rationale.vehicle: All direct custom-design benefits in this feat apply to starships, which are vehicles.
rationale.durability: Improve Hull directly adds starship hit points.
rationale.shields: Improve Shields directly increases shield rating.
rationale.weapon_empowerment: Improve Weapons directly enhances a starship weapon.
rationale.precision: Improve Weapons grants a +1 equipment bonus on attack rolls.

adjudicationNotes: Do not preserve current metadata strings design or starship as semantic tags; neither is in the frozen 181-tag vocabulary.
Do not add pilot merely because starships are piloted or because related character routes often use Pilot; the Benefit does not modify Pilot checks.
Do not add mobility for the hyperdrive customization: the printed option changes hyperdrive class rather than tactical movement speed.

assignments.name: Starship Tactics
assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Adds 1 + Wisdom modifier starship maneuvers to the character's maneuver suite, allows repeat selection of the feat and repeated maneuver choices, and grants additional maneuvers when Wisdom modifier permanently increases.
assignments.existingTagsAuthority: data/feat_buckets_and_subbuckets.json metadataTags on current default branch; informational only, not semantic authority

rationale.vehicle: The granted suite consists of starship maneuvers used in vehicle-scale starship combat.
rationale.space: The feat grants the starship-maneuver subsystem used for space combat.
rationale.tactics: The feat grants tactical starship maneuvers rather than a generic skill or attack bonus.
rationale.resources: Starship maneuvers form a finite suite of expendable/recoverable maneuver uses.
rationale.scaling: The number of maneuvers granted scales with Wisdom modifier, repeat feat acquisition, and later permanent Wisdom-modifier increases.

adjudicationNotes: pilot is not retained solely from the printed prerequisite. The Benefit grants a maneuver suite that can include pilot and gunner maneuvers, so pilot would be narrower than the actual mechanic.
No starship_maneuver tag is created. vehicle + space + tactics + resources expresses the semantic role within the frozen ontology without material loss.

assignments.name: Tactical Genius
assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: At the end of any round in which the character rolls a natural 20 on an attack roll, all spent starship maneuvers are regained.
assignments.existingTagsAuthority: data/feat_buckets_and_subbuckets.json metadataTags on current default branch; informational only, not semantic authority

rationale.vehicle: The recovered resources are starship maneuvers in the vehicle-combat subsystem.
rationale.space: The mechanic operates on the starship-maneuver suite used for space combat.
rationale.tactics: The feat restores tactical starship maneuvers.
rationale.resource_recovery: The Benefit restores all spent maneuver resources.
rationale.critical_success: The recovery trigger is a natural 20 on an attack roll.
rationale.pilot: The feat's Normal rule explicitly defines starship-maneuver recovery through a natural 20 on a Pilot check; Tactical Genius expands that same recovery mechanic with an attack-roll trigger.

adjudicationNotes: Do not use critical_hit: the feat does not alter critical-hit damage or critical-hit effects; it keys off the natural-20 success trigger.
Do not add pilot from the prerequisite. The printed trigger is any qualifying attack roll and the recovered suite is broader than Pilot checks.
Do not preserve current metadata string starship as a semantic tag; it is not in the frozen vocabulary.

qualityControl.label: QC1_DEEP_REVIEW_AFTER_9_BOOKS

semanticReconciliations.name: Tech Specialist
semanticReconciliations.reason: Tech Specialist modifies existing equipment; the certified talent ontology uses `crafting` for creation/fabrication mechanics, while modification-only mechanics use `modification`.

semanticReconciliations.name: Suppression Fire
semanticReconciliations.reason: Direct talent convergence: suppression through Aid Another is a teamwork/support mechanic aimed at a specific enemy; certified suppression talents use teamwork/targeting for the same behavior.

semanticReconciliations.name: Force Regimen Mastery
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit directly teaches Force regimens; certified Regimen Aptitude uses `force_training` for Force-regimen training semantics.

semanticReconciliations.name: Multi-Targeting
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit directly changes how the swift actions required to aim may be distributed across rounds, so it is an action-timing/action-economy mechanic.

semanticReconciliations.name: Attack Combo (Ranged)
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit explicitly says qualifying later ranged attacks include attacks of opportunity.

semanticReconciliations.name: Biotech Specialist
semanticReconciliations.reason: Biotech Specialist modifies existing biotech objects; it does not itself create/fabricate them. Keep `modification`, not the creation-oriented `crafting` tag.

semanticReconciliations.name: Brink of Death
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit changes lethal damage into a nonlethal 0-hp outcome; `nonlethal` and `damage` express the mechanic without using the broader enemy-control concept.

semanticReconciliations.name: Rancor Crush
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit moves a pinned target down the condition track when Pin+Crush succeeds; it does not reference, modify, or test Damage Threshold.

semanticReconciliations.name: Returning Bug
semanticReconciliations.reason: Returning a missed thrown weapon preserves equipment; it does not stabilize the attack result. `reliability` is reserved for rerolls/take-10/automatic-success/failure-rescue-like outcome stabilization.

semanticReconciliations.name: Vehicle Systems Expertise
semanticReconciliations.reason: One of the two vehicle actions directly accelerated by the feat is Recharge Shields, so the feat materially improves access to shield-resource recovery.

semanticReconciliations.name: Implant Training
semanticReconciliations.reason: The feat prevents the implant's extra condition-track step whenever the character moves down the track; no Damage Threshold test or modification is involved.

semanticReconciliations.name: Mandalorian Training
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit explicitly grants a +2 morale bonus to Will Defense while using Charging Fire.

semanticReconciliations.name: Sniper Shot
semanticReconciliations.reason: The mechanical Benefit is a ranged attack/Reflex-defense tradeoff and has no aim, range, or sniper-specific mechanic. Keeping `sniper` here would be name-driven.

semanticReconciliations.name: Advantageous Attack
semanticReconciliations.reason: The feat keys off an enemy that has not yet acted but does not modify Initiative; certified talent analogues treat this as ambush timing rather than an Initiative mechanic.

semanticReconciliations.name: Angled Throw
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit applies to grenades and grenadelike weapons. Those are not improvised weapons by this feat's mechanic.

semanticReconciliations.name: Bad Feeling
semanticReconciliations.reason: Direct convergence with certified Surprisingly Quick: both grant otherwise-unavailable action capacity in the surprise round even when surprised.

semanticReconciliations.name: Controlled Rage
semanticReconciliations.reason: The feat changes rage activation/termination timing; the shared `control` tag is used for target/battlefield/social control, not ordinary self-regulation.

semanticReconciliations.name: Focused Rage
semanticReconciliations.reason: The Benefit permits concentration/patience skills while raging at a penalty; `skills` captures the mechanic without misusing target/battlefield `control`.

semanticReconciliations.name: Swarm
semanticReconciliations.reason: Adjacent allies enable the user's own melee attack bonus; the feat does not grant a benefit to those allies. Keep `teamwork`, not ally-support semantics.

semanticReconciliations.name: Droid Hunter
semanticReconciliations.reason: The mechanic is a damage bonus against droids, not an aim/designation/target-acquisition mechanic; `droid` + `damage_bonus` are sufficient.

semanticReconciliations.name: Separatist Military Training
semanticReconciliations.reason: Adjacency to an ally enables the user's own attack bonus; the feat does not support or buff the ally. `teamwork` and `positioning` remain.

semanticReconciliations.name: Hyperblazer
semanticReconciliations.reason: Halving time and penalties is not a reroll/take-10/automatic-success/fixed-result/failure-rescue mechanic; the certified ontology explicitly excludes generic time/action compression from `reliability`.

semanticReconciliations.name: Intimidator
semanticReconciliations.reason: Neither the feat Benefit nor the Core Intimidate application labels this effect mind-affecting. Do not infer the descriptor from Persuasion/Intimidate alone.

semanticReconciliations.name: Momentum Strike
semanticReconciliations.reason: Threats of the Galaxy explicitly publishes these under NEW RIDING FEATS; this is structural metadata, separate from semantic tags.

semanticReconciliations.name: Mounted Defense
semanticReconciliations.reason: Threats of the Galaxy explicitly publishes these under NEW RIDING FEATS; this is structural metadata, separate from semantic tags.

corrections.reason: The feat's Normal rule explicitly defines starship-maneuver recovery through a natural 20 on a Pilot check; Tactical Genius expands that same recovery mechanic with an attack-roll trigger.
The Benefit explicitly causes automatic success on Endurance checks to restore shield rating and changes the timing of that Endurance-based recovery action.

The Benefit applies to trained Strength-based skill checks; in the Core skill system this bounded group includes Climb, Jump, and Swim. The Special clause explicitly requires an Endurance check for an additional use.
The Benefit rerolls trained Strength- and Constitution-based skill checks. The bounded Core skill group is Climb, Jump, Swim, and Endurance.
The Benefit explicitly increases Climb speed, Swim speed, and Jump distance.
The Benefit directly increases the DC of an opponent's Acrobatics check to tumble through a threatened square.
The Benefit explicitly preserves Acrobatics checks to tumble as the remaining means of escaping threatened squares.
The Benefit directly substitutes Perception for Gather Information, grants training for that use, inherits Gather Information rerolls, and reduces Gather Information time.
The Benefit grants a bonus to Strength-based skill checks; in the Core skill system the bounded Strength-based skill group is Climb, Jump, and Swim.

The Benefit requires scavenged materials to be applied to construction through the Build Object application of the Mechanics skill, making Mechanics part of the feat's actual downstream mechanic rather than merely a prerequisite.
The Benefit directly imposes a penalty on skill checks used to negate the user's next attack. No particular skill is singled out, so the generic `skills` tag is correct.
The Benefit directly modifies defenses against attacks or effects requiring a Use the Force check. The shared invariant `use_the_force -> force` therefore also applies.
The Benefit explicitly requires a DC 20 Acrobatics check to move the ally.
The Benefit substitutes Knowledge for Wisdom or Wisdom-related checks. For skill checks, the bounded Core Wisdom-based skill group includes Perception, Survival, and Treat Injury.
The Benefit directly penalizes affected enemies' skill checks against the user, but does not single out a particular skill.
The Benefit directly sets the observer's opposed Perception check against both the user's Deception and Stealth checks.
The Benefit requires the mount to make a DC 20 Endurance check before subsequent attempts to spur it during the encounter.

skillTagPolicy.specificSkillRule: Add the exact skill tag when the feat directly uses, modifies, substitutes, rerolls, changes timing for, resists, or otherwise interacts with that skill.
skillTagPolicy.boundedSkillFamilyRule: When source text targets a deterministic bounded ability-based skill family, add each affected skill tag.
skillTagPolicy.genericSkillRule: When the mechanic applies to any/all skills without specializing them, use `skills` instead of all individual skill tags.
skillTagPolicy.parentApplicationRule: Named applications inherit the parent skill tag (for example Intimidate -> persuasion; Sleight of Hand -> stealth).
